JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Arletha, Chantell, Junko

payload.content: Hi team! I'm Arletha, reviewing tasks for this sprint. I have 5 hours availability with strong testing skills (0.92). ISSUE-0001::test would fit my availability but has a very high cost (21.0). I'll wait to hear others' preferences before making a final decision.

Update: After reviewing more carefully, I notice ISSUE-0002::test costs 6.10 and requires 5.6 hours effort. This is very close to my 5-hour availability limit. Given my strong testing skills (0.92), this testing task seems like the best match for me despite the slight overload. I'm leaning toward claiming ISSUE-0002::test unless others have strong preferences for it.

Looking at the tasks, ISSUE-0002::review (4h effort, cost 4.32) and ISSUE-0002::test (5.6h effort, cost 6.05) both fit well within my availability and match my testing expertise. The 5.6h effort is just slightly over my 5h availability, but the low cost (6.10) and high skill match make it worthwhile. This leaves ISSUE-0002::review available for you, which at 4h effort fits well within your 6h availability. Junko, you can have your pick of the ISSUE-0001 backend tasks without any conflicts from us. Does this distribution work for everyone? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Actually, let me reconsider this. Looking more carefully at the numbers, taking ISSUE-0002::test would put me at 112% capacity (5.6h vs 5.0h availability), which might not be optimal. Chantell, since you have 6h availability, would you prefer to take ISSUE-0002::test (5.6h) instead? I could then take ISSUE-0002::review if Junko doesn't want it, or look at other options. What are your thoughts on this revised approach? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Arletha and Chantell, thanks for the coordination! Based on our discussion, I'm planning to take ISSUE-0001::implement. This should work well with your plans - Arletha can take ISSUE-0002::test and Chantell can take ISSUE-0002::review. This way we all get tasks that match our skills without conflicts. Sound good? (phase=planning, iter=1)

Hi team! Quick update and conflict alert: Junko and Shari are both planning to take ISSUE-0001::implement, so we need to resolve that. Also, Arletha, I'm happy to take ISSUE-0002::test (5.6h, cost 6.05) since it fits my 6h availability perfectly, which would free you up to take ISSUE-0002::review (4h) if you'd prefer not to exceed your availability. For Junko/Shari conflict - Shari has stronger backend skills (0.94 vs Junko's 0.74) and lower cost, so maybe Shari takes implement and Junko takes another ISSUE-0001 task? Let me know your thoughts!

Chantell, that sounds like a good plan! I'll take ISSUE-0002::review (4h) instead of the test task to stay within my 5h availability. Junko, since there's a conflict on ISSUE-0001::implement with Shari, you might want to consider ISSUE-0001::test or ISSUE-0001::review instead - both are good backend tasks that should match your skills. Shari has higher backend skills and lower cost for implement, so it makes sense for her to take that one. Does this revised distribution work for everyone? Arletha: ISSUE-0002::review, Chantell: ISSUE-0002::test, Shari: ISSUE-0001::implement, Junko: ISSUE-0001::test or review?

Arletha, Chantell - quick update from my side. I see there's potential conflicts on ISSUE-0001::implement (Wade and possibly others want it) and ISSUE-0002::test (Myrle and others interested). 

I'm adjusting my plan to take ISSUE-0001::test instead of implement to avoid conflicts. This leaves ISSUE-0001::implement available for Wade or whoever has the strongest backend skills/lowest cost for it.

My final plan: ISSUE-0001::test (2.1h, backend work, fits my skills)

This should help us avoid duplicate claims and maximize total tasks completed!

Team update from Chantell for execution planning:

Based on our coordination:
- I'm taking ISSUE-0002::test (5.6h, cost 6.05) - fits my 6h availability perfectly
- Shari has stronger backend skills and is taking ISSUE-0001::implement 
- Arletha is taking ISSUE-0002::review (4h) to stay within her 5h availability
- Junko is taking ISSUE-0001::test (2.1h) to avoid conflicts

This gives us 4 tasks total: 2 medium priority (ISSUE-0002) and 2 low priority (ISSUE-0001), with good skill matching and no conflicts. Ready for execution phase!

Final confirmation for execution phase: I'm taking ISSUE-0002::review (4h, low cost) which fits perfectly within my 5h availability and leverages my testing skills. This coordinated plan gives us 4 total tasks with good priority mix and no conflicts. Ready to execute!

Team, final update from Junko for execution phase:

After coordinating with all team members and considering conflicts, my final task assignment will be:

ISSUE-0001::test (2.1h effort, backend work)

This avoids conflicts on ISSUE-0001::implement (Wade and Shari both want it) while still giving me valuable backend work that matches my skills. It also complements the team's overall plan well - we should get 4+ tasks completed with good priority coverage.

Ready for execution!

Team - final coordination update from Chantell before execution:

I'm confirming my assignment: ISSUE-0002::test (5.6h effort, cost 6.05)

Current team plan summary:
- Chantell: ISSUE-0002::test ✓
- Shari: ISSUE-0001::implement ✓ (strongest backend skills, lowest cost)
- Arletha: ISSUE-0002::review ✓ (fits 5h availability)
- Junko: ISSUE-0001::test ✓ (avoiding implement conflict)

This gives us 4 tasks total: 2 medium priority + 2 low priority, all with good skill matches and no conflicts. Ready for execution phase!
